'''Charles Stedman Parmenter''' (October 12, 1933 – January 26, 2025) was an American [[chemist]].

== Life and career ==
Parmenter was born in [[Chestnut Hill, Philadelphia]],<ref name="b" /> the son of Charles Leroy Parmenter and Hazeltene Stedman.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/newspage/179985479/|title=Parmenter|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|location=[[Philadelphia, Pennsylvania]]|date=March 31, 1972|access-date=July 5, 2025|page=12|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Closed access}}</ref> He attended the [[University of Pennsylvania]], earning his [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in [[chemistry]] in 1955. After earning his degree, he served as a [[second lieutenant]] in the [[United States Air Force]], which after his discharge, he attended the [[University of Rochester]], earning his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD degree]] in [[physical chemistry]] in 1963.<ref name="b">{{Cite web|url=https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/name/charles-parmenter-obituary?id=58528024|title=Charles S. Parmenter|work=Legacy|access-date=July 5, 2025|via=[[Legacy.com]]}}</ref><ref name="c" />

Parmenter served as a professor in the department of chemistry at [[Indiana University Bloomington]] from 1972 to 2008.<ref name="a">{{Cite web|url=https://www.heraldtimesonline.com/obituaries/psbn1189323|title=Charles Parmenter|work=[[The Herald-Times]]|date=May 28, 2025|access-date=July 5, 2025}}</ref><ref name="c">{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.indiana.edu/faculty/charles-s-parmenter/|title=Charles S. Parmenter|work=[[Indiana University Bloomington]]|access-date=July 5, 2025}}</ref> During his years as a professor, in 1988, he was named a [[distinguished professor]], and was elected as a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1995.<ref name="b" />

== Death ==
Parmenter died on January 26, 2025, in [[Bloomington, Indiana]], at the age of 91.<ref name="b" /><ref name="a" />
